intro: Maine runs its elections town by town and city by city, through each municipal clerk or registrar of voters.

id_rule.text: If you are already registered, you do not need to show ID to get a ballot. If you register on Election Day, you must register in person and show ID and proof of where you live. Anyone without ID can still vote a challenged ballot.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Opening times vary by town, between 6:00 am and 10:00 am; all polls close at 8:00 pm
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Absentee voting at the clerk's office
dates.detail: Absentee ballots are available at your town or city clerk's office starting 30 days before Election Day. You do not need an application if you vote in person there. In-person absentee voting ends on the Thursday before Election Day, Oct. 29, unless special circumstances apply.

src.label: Maine Secretary of State, State of Maine voter guide

dates.label: Last day to register online or by mail
dates.detail: Online registration closes at 5 pm. Mailed forms must reach your town or city by the end of the business day (21 days before Election Day). You can still register in person at your clerk's office up to the close of the polls on Election Day.

src.label: Maine Secretary of State, State of Maine voter guide

dates.label: Last day to register at the Motor Vehicle office
dates.detail: Registration through the Bureau of Motor Vehicles closes 7 days before Election Day.

src.label: Maine Secretary of State, State of Maine voter guide

dates.label: Absentee ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Your town or city clerk must receive your request by the end of the business day (3 business days before Election Day), unless special circumstances apply. Maine does not require a reason to vote absentee.

src.label: Maine Secretary of State, State of Maine voter guide
Maine Secretary of State, absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls close at 8 pm. An absentee ballot must reach your municipal clerk by 8 pm. You can register in person and vote on Election Day.
